status: read-only audit; 60 registered Property Declarations inspected

coverage.method: Read each register entry classified Property; scanned its Claim for graph endpoint expressions; reviewed Node common Rules and Relation Definitions.

subject_focus: A Declaration constrains its active Subject's outgoing degree only. Inverse outgoing degree belongs to the counterpart Declaration. Omitted foreign endpoint bounds are not local gaps.

effective_common_constraints.direction_target: Property -> immediate Node bearer; HAS_PROPERTY is derived inverse.
effective_common_constraints.formal_status: Endpoint is formal but exact-one is not: declare-node.md:25-32 permits {:0..1}, while the definition says one bearer.
effective_common_constraints.action: Add one shared exact-one bearing constraint, inherited by all 60; do not repeat it locally.

effective_common_constraints.formal_status: No Property-local reverse degree is needed. Nested Properties use the same shared bearing rule.
Property Nodes are prohibited: the one-bearing-link branch requires HAS_NARROWER zero.
Property Nodes are prohibited from instances by HAS_INSTANCE zero.
Literal binding, not a Node-to-Node relation; it grants no graph endpoint, inverse, instance, or bearer.

effective_common_constraints.owning_subject: Node -> applicable Axis / scalar value test
effective_common_constraints.formal_status: Independence classification is used by common Node rules. `in (...)` is scalar membership, not a graph edge; neither grants generic Property relations.

approved_positive_grants.scope: Property -> immediate bearer, with derived reverse.
approved_positive_grants.caveat: Needs the common exact-one cardinality repair.
Its own outgoing degree belongs in the Event Record Declaration, not Event Record.Relations.HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR Property.

value_not_edge_findings.finding: Formats [Actor//], [atom id], and [scope unit] constrain direct values only. They do not grant HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR or IS_CONTAINED_BY edges.
`.*[Relation//]{:0+}` permits relation-named child Property names; it is not a graph-relation whitelist and grants no edge.

actionable_gaps.problem: Property bearing has prose exact-one semantics but only formal {:0..1}.
actionable_gaps.counterexample: A zero-bearing-link Node follows the Primary branch even though the Property-bearing definition describes every Property as having one bearer.
actionable_gaps.smallest_fix: One shared Property -> bearer {:1} constraint; no 60-file expansion.

actionable_gaps.scope: Event Record and Atom Primary relation-whitelist design
actionable_gaps.problem: The relation-named Property values do not formally map to graph edges. The HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR endpoint definition alone neither establishes a Property mapping nor selects the whitelist encoding.
actionable_gaps.counterexample: A Property can hold an Actor reference with no edge, or an endpoint can permit an edge without that value Property.
actionable_gaps.required_choice: Choose signature-based closed whitelists or a separate explicit whitelist expression. Then place each actual edge's outgoing signature/cardinality on its active Primary subject (Event Record or Atom), not on the child Property.

local_additions_assessment.all_60: No Property-local graph relation is justified solely by a Property path, prose mention, relation-like child name, or typed reference format.
local_additions_assessment.inheritance: Effective whitelist resolution reuses inherited constraints; it must not redeclare inherited Properties or actual facts.
local_additions_assessment.pending_architecture: Signature-based closed whitelist versus separate explicit whitelist expression is an open user choice; this report assumes neither.
